questions.question: A low-pressure chiller needs an oil change. The work is not major, and the chiller will not be evacuated to the atmosphere afterward. What pressure limit does 40 CFR 82.156 set before the chiller is opened for the oil change?

options.A: Evacuated or pressurized to no higher than 10 psig
options.B: Evacuated or pressurized to no higher than 15 psig
options.C: Evacuated or pressurized to no higher than 5 psig
options.D: Evacuated or pressurized to no higher than 25 psig

questions.explanation: For oil changes the appliance must "be evacuated or pressurized to a pressure no higher than 5 psig, before it is opened". The rule also allows draining the oil "into a system receiver to be evacuated or pressurized to a pressure no higher than 5 psig."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: For the purposes of oil changes, be evacuated or pressurized to a pressure no higher than 5 psig, before it is opened; or drain the oil into a system receiver to be evacuated or pressurized to a pressure no higher than 5 psig.

questions.question: Leaks in a low-pressure chiller would substantially contaminate the refrigerant being recovered. To what level must the leaking components that will be opened be evacuated?

options.A: No lower than atmospheric pressure
options.B: The lowest level that can be attained without substantially contaminating the refrigerant, and no higher than 0 psig
options.C: To 5 psig or lower
options.D: Whatever level the recovery machine reaches in 15 minutes

questions.explanation: Persons must "Evacuate leaking components to be opened or disposed of to the lowest level that can be attained without substantially contaminating the refrigerant. This level may not exceed 0 psig." Non-leaking components still go to the Table 1 levels.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Evacuate leaking components to be opened or disposed of to the lowest level that can be attained without substantially contaminating the refrigerant. This level may not exceed 0 psig.

questions.question: A technician will remove the condenser from a low-pressure chiller to replace it. The chiller will not be evacuated to the atmosphere after the work. What must the technician do before opening it?

options.A: Pressurize it to no higher than 0 psig, because the chiller will not be evacuated to the atmosphere afterward
options.B: Pressurize it to no higher than 5 psig
options.C: Cover the openings and use nitrogen to bring it to atmospheric pressure
options.D: Evacuate the refrigerant to the Table 1 level (25 mm Hg absolute), because removing the condenser is a major repair

questions.explanation: A major repair is one that "involves the removal of any or all of the following appliance components: compressor, condenser, evaporator, or auxiliary heat exchange coil". The 0 psig option applies only "if the maintenance, service, or repair is not major as defined at § 82.152", so the Table 1 level applies.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Major maintenance, service, or repair means any maintenance, service, or repair that involves the removal of any or all of the following appliance components: compressor, condenser, evaporator, or auxiliary heat exchange coil

questions.question: A repair on a low-pressure chiller removes no compressor, condenser, evaporator or auxiliary heat exchange coil, but it will uncover a 6-square-inch flow-area opening for about 20 minutes. How does 40 CFR 82.152 classify this repair?

options.A: As major maintenance, service, or repair
options.B: As not major, because no major component is removed
options.C: As an oil change
options.D: As not major, because the opening lasts less than 30 minutes

questions.explanation: Major repair also includes "any maintenance, service, or repair that involves uncovering an opening of more than four (4) square inches of “flow area” for more than 15 minutes." A 6-square-inch opening for 20 minutes meets both limits, so the 0 psig pressurizing option for non-major repairs is not available.

options.C: When the refrigerant in the part can be isolated to a system receiver
options.D: When the work will be finished within 15 minutes
